messages.body_plain:
The stats package functionality is no longer included in renjin-core as of 0.7.0. If you want all of the 'default' packages like stats, utils, graphics, etc., then just make sure your project references the renjin-script-engine artifact rather than just renjin-core.

I've updated the wiki to reflect this change:

https://code.google.com/p/renjin/wiki/CallingRFromJava

Alex

On Apr 4, 2013 2:30 PM, <abh...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I am trying to call a custom R script (already provided by some other team)  from Java. How do I do that using Renjin? I see that there is an article
> which suggests this.
>
> // create a script engine manager
>
>
>
> ScriptEngineManager factory = new ScriptEngineManager();
>
> // create an R engine
>
>
>
> ScriptEngine engine = factory.getEngineByName("Renjin");
>
>
>
> // evaluate R code from String
>
> engine.eval("print('Hello, World')");
>
> // evaluate R script on disk
> engine.eval(new FileReader("myscript.R"));
>
>
>
>
> // evaluate R script from classpath
> engine.eval(new InputStreamReader(
>    getClass().getResourceAsStream("myScript.R")));
>
>
>
>
>
> However, I am getting a NullPointerException at
>
> engine.eval("print('Hello, World')");
>
>
>
>
> since the engine evaluated in the previous line is null.
>
> Any help will be appreciated.
>
> Thanks,
>
